elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 14 (unchanged) presupposes an unconditional Client exit: "TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement." The election is not conditioned on breach or cause, so it operates as a convenience right even though the words "for convenience" are absent (which is why the 'Customer convenience termination present' regex returned false).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 14 runs services "until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides ... notice", i.e. an effective wind-down of roughly 30–60 days depending on the notice date; there is no flat 30-day cap. To reach preferred the drafter would have to state "Client may terminate this Agreement or any service upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice."

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic appears in the rendered text. Section 5(a) only says TrueLink invoices "on a monthly basis" and "Invoices will be paid within 15 days of receipt", which does not state whether the monthly invoice covers the coming or the completed month, so the 'no prepaid fees' condition is not established on the face of the clause. Preferred would require an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: As redlined, TrueLink's only no-cause exit is non-renewal at the end of a one-year period ("or TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days, prior to the end of said year"); the mid-term terminations in Section 13 are cause-based (Client breach of System/Credit Repository Agreements or Sections 8a–8c). Residual check: Section 12, cross-referenced but not rendered, must not contain a TrueLink at-will right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 14 gives Client a no-cause exit effective the last day of the month following the notice month (~30–60 days), which is within and in fact better than the 60–90 day fallback window; existing favourable language was correctly left untouched.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty or unamortised-cost recovery appears in the term, termination or fee provisions. Section 5(a) provides only monthly invoicing against Exhibits A/B with a monthly minimum ("not less than $____ per month"), which is a running charge rather than a termination charge, so there is nothing to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 confines TrueLink's no-cause exit to end-of-term non-renewal: "unless Client delivers to TrueLink written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days, or TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days, prior to the end of said year." No TrueLink mid-term convenience right survives in the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days ... prior to the end of said year" imposes a minimum 90-day lead time (notice must land at least 90 days before term end), curing the prior mutual 30-day trigger.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all four fallback elements are met on the rendered operative language — Client's Section 14 no-cause exit (~30–60 days, better than the 60–90 window), no early-termination fee anywhere to cap, and TrueLink's exit now confined to end-of-term non-renewal on at least 90 days' notice.

Preferred is not reached and should not be claimed: Section 14 gives a 30–60 day wind-down rather than a flat 30-day notice, and there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. If the drafter wants preferred, the operative fix is (i) "Client may terminate this Agreement or any Service upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice" and (ii) "TrueLink shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination." The mapping's assertion that nothing is prepaid is inference from monthly invoicing, not operative text — Section 5(a) does not say invoices are issued in arrears.

The 'Customer convenience termination present' regex failed only because Section 14 never uses "for convenience" or "without cause"; in substance it is an unconditional Client election to terminate, so the element stands. Clarifying wording would be optional polish, not required, and adding it would go beyond the minimal fallback set.

Deviation status is correct: pre-redline, TrueLink could decline renewal on thirty (30) days' notice, which is squarely in the playbook's walk-away band (Vendor convenience exit on fewer than 90 days' notice) and leaves no realistic migration window for hosting and credit-data services.

Minimal: the edit touches one sentence of Section 13, splits the previously mutual 30-day non-renewal trigger, preserves Client's favourable 30-day notice and Section 14 right, adds no new obligations, and does not duplicate any operative term. Section 5(a) is cited as evidence only and is unamended.

Intent preserved: the one-year term, automatic successive renewals, the Section 12 termination cross-reference, the cause-based mid-term cut-offs, migration timelines (30/60 days) and payment mechanics all survive without contradiction; the resulting asymmetry favours us and is intentional.

Residual diligence for the drafter (not a defect in the rendered text): confirm that Section 12 and Section 4 (both cross-referenced but not rendered) contain no TrueLink at-will termination right or termination charge, since either would undercut fallback elements 2–4.
